title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 42 (Issue of shares on private placement basis)

content.overview: Section 42 permits a company, subject to its provisions, to make a private placement of securities only to a select group of persons identified by the Board (identified persons). Their number shall not exceed fifty or such higher number as may be prescribed, excluding qualified institutional buyers and employees offered securities under a scheme of employees stock option under section 62(1)(b), in a financial year, subject to prescribed conditions. The company shall issue private placement offer and application in the prescribed form and manner to identified persons whose names and addresses are recorded as prescribed; the offer and application shall not carry any right of renunciation. Explanation: private placement means any offer or invitation to subscribe or issue of securities to a select group of persons by a company (other than by way of public offer) through private placement offer-cum-application which satisfies the conditions specified in this section. Every identified person shall apply along with subscription money paid by cheque, demand draft or other banking channel and not by cash. The company shall allot the securities within sixty days from the date of receipt of the application money; if it fails, it shall repay the application money within fifteen days from the expiry of sixty days, and if it fails to so repay, it shall be liable to repay with interest at twelve per cent per annum from the expiry of the sixtieth day. Application money shall be kept in a separate bank account in a scheduled bank. A return of allotment shall be filed.
content.glance: Private placement only to Board-identified persons within the numerical cap (excluding QIBs and s.62 ESOP employees); prescribed offer with no renunciation; banking-channel payment; allot within 60 days or refund with 12% interest.
content.study: A private placement is an offer or invitation to a select group of Board-identified persons (other than by public offer) through a private placement offer-cum-application satisfying section 42. The number of identified persons in a financial year must not exceed fifty or the prescribed higher number, excluding QIBs and employees under an ESOP scheme under section 62(1)(b). The offer and application must be in the prescribed form to recorded identified persons and must not carry a right of renunciation. Subscription money must be paid through banking channels, not cash. Securities must be allotted within sixty days of receipt of application money, failing which the money must be repaid within fifteen days of the expiry of sixty days, with interest at twelve per cent per annum from the expiry of the sixtieth day if not so repaid. Application money must be kept in a separate bank account. A return of allotment must be filed. Current-law framing: identify the offer; test identified persons and numerical cap; check form, payment channel, 60-day allotment/refund and separate account.

sections.heading: Private placement meaning
sections.body: Offer or invitation to a select group of persons other than by way of public offer, through private placement offer-cum-application satisfying the section.

sections.heading: Identified persons and numerical cap
sections.body: Board-identified persons; number not exceeding fifty or such higher number as prescribed per financial year, excluding QIBs and employees under s. 62(1)(b) ESOP.

sections.heading: Offer form and no renunciation
sections.body: Prescribed private placement offer and application to recorded identified persons; shall not carry any right of renunciation.

sections.heading: Payment, allotment and refund
sections.body: Subscription money by banking channel (not cash); allot within 60 days of receipt of application money or repay within 15 days thereafter, with 12% interest from expiry of the 60th day if unpaid.

sections.heading: Separate account and return of allotment
sections.body: Application money kept in a separate bank account in a scheduled bank; return of allotment to be filed.

provisions.title: issue of shares on private placement basis

examples.title: Compliant private placement
examples.body: Board identifies persons within the statutory cap, issues prescribed offer-cum-application without renunciation, receives banking-channel money into a separate account, allots within 60 days and files the return of allotment.

examples.title: Late refund interest
examples.body: If securities are not allotted within 60 days and application money is not repaid within the further 15 days, interest at 12% per annum runs from the expiry of the sixtieth day.

hypotheticals.question: Does an offer to 60 persons automatically breach section 42?
hypotheticals.analysis: Not necessarily. The statutory ceiling is fifty or such higher number as may be prescribed (excluding QIBs and specified ESOP employees). Apply the current prescribed number and the exclusions.

misconceptions.trap: Private placement has no numerical limit.
misconceptions.correction: Section 42 caps the number of identified persons per financial year (fifty or prescribed higher number, excluding QIBs and specified ESOP employees).

misconceptions.trap: Identified persons may freely renounce the offer.
misconceptions.correction: The private placement offer and application shall not carry any right of renunciation.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 42 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify whether the offer is a private placement (select group, not public offer). II. Test Board identification, numerical cap and exclusions. III. Check prescribed form, no renunciation, banking-channel payment, 60-day allotment/refund and separate account. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Facts; statutory ingredients of s. 42; applicable exclusions and prescribed limits; precise relief or compliance finding.
